indexing: Life/examples step indexes are zero-based; outline numbered acts keep their written numbers, with frame act 0. fields names top-level JSON metadata.

rulings.defect: Consent authenticates by repeatedly posting Maya’s password, and the served form carries that password as a hidden field. There is no captured signed-in browser session. The documented screen identity contract requires an opaque cookie, not a credential resubmitted in each consent form.
rulings.requiredChange: At step 4 authenticate Maya through the pack’s sign-in flow, capture its opaque Set-Cookie, and obtain the consent page as that session. At step 5 submit the consent with the captured session cookie and no email/password credential fields. If a distinct sign-in request is needed, insert it at these named steps. Keep client/state/callback parameters and validate returned state.

rulings.defect: Later requests type literal BOOK-2 or BOOK-1 from the twin’s numbering sequence even though the create responses are the source of those identifiers. Captured UUIDs exist but the requested shorthand ids are not captured.
rulings.requiredChange: Capture firstIdentifier and secondIdentifier from the corresponding issueCreate.issue.identifier at 14 and 15. Replace request literals in step 19 with {secondIdentifier} and steps 28 and 35 with {firstIdentifier}. Literal names used as prose labels are harmless; only request values must derive from the answers.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects

rulings.defect: The step promises to resume the support report, but its entire request is viewer { id }. It only verifies the replacement token’s identity and reads no report data.
rulings.requiredChange: Use the refreshed {at} to actually obtain the report’s issue/context, such as issue(id:{i1}) with title/state/comments, and assert the known booking finding, reopened state and Safari comment. Preserve or include viewer in the same query if identity verification remains needed. The step must fulfill the named reporting action.
rulings.source: ../twin-world/docs/contributing/architecture.md: Published examples and What a judge rejects

doubts.doubt: Entity already archived is explicitly admitted to be the twin’s chosen message, not a vendor-published refusal. The vendor only documents a standard GraphQL error envelope. There is no published contradiction sufficient for a ruling; the assertion does not independently prove vendor fidelity.

The walk defaults to 2026-01-01 while the vendored schema was committed 2026-09-28. No source dates the actual used fields after January, so no wrong-era ruling is justified. Next morning after 1h+8h falls at 09:00 on the initial day; avoid reading the name as an explicit calendar-day assertion.
The new worker’s label lookup does not feed a label id into a subsequent mutation, but a worker initialization/discovery need is stated, so it is not demonstrably a needless read.

notes: Read the complete outline, all 44 customer-life steps, all 34 examples steps, all 33 vendored documentation example entries, and every one of 11 notReplayed reasons. Reviewed the SDL fields/inputs and vendor pages for GraphQL, pagination, filtering, OAuth, OAuth actor authorization, and deprecations. No suite reruns and no pack implementation/story edits.

Every bar item was applied: refusal causes; repeats and sitting boundaries; state toggles; kept promises; feature-tour padding; read need; actors and learned identifiers; era; vendor contradictions; payload/name fidelity; and documented doors.

The reported green checks were treated as orientation only, not proof of plausibility. No second judging is requested: the author must apply this complete ruling set once and carry the verdict mechanically.
